title: Overnight escalation scrub & handoff (cache-fallthrough) 2026-06-01
body:
Purpose:
Notes from the overnight shift (11:45pm PDT -> 7:30am PDT) summarizing the cache-related latency spike, actions taken, and follow-ups for the day team. This doc is a handoff for incoming daytime oncall and a working draft of a runbook addition.

Summary (TL;DR):
- 00:12 UTC (17:12 PDT) large increase in tail latency for /v1/generate from ~120ms p50 -> ~1.9s p95; error rate remained low (~0.2% 5xx).
- Root cause (hypothesis): concurrent Redis prefix eviction + cold KV-cache loads causing a cascade to fallback routing to smaller-capacity CPU-serving pool.
- Mitigation: throttled cache-filling scripts, temporarily increased GPU pool capacity by enabling reserved-burst (dedicated autoscale policy), and rolled ephemeral circuit-breaker to delay fallback for 30s.
- Impact: user-facing latency elevated for ~42 minutes for a bounded subset of tenants; no data loss.

Timeline & key actions (timestamps in PDT):
- 23:45 (oncall start): baseline check, no anomalies.
- 00:12: alert: latency-slo-service:gateway p95 > 1.5s for route /v1/generate (alert SLO-LAT-011). Pager triggered.
- 00:14: verified elevated tail latency via /console/metrics and quick kql: "latency_ms|route=/v1/generate|p95".
- 00:16: checked GPU utilization: healthy; CPU-serving pool had spikes. Noted increased calls to fallback route (fallback-to-cpu=true).
- 00:20: examined Redis metrics (cache-primary-az1): eviction_count increased sharply; memory usage near max for a 3m window.
- 00:22: paused nightly cache-warm job (cron id: tools/cache-warm-3am) to stop further cold loads. (command: gcloud scheduler jobs pause cache-warm-3am --project=infra-prod)
body_continued:
- 00:25: enabled reserved-burst on GPU pool (policy: dedicated:burst-50pct) via infra console to absorb short-term load; verified new pods scaled and started accepting traffic.
- 00:30: implemented short-circuit: increased fallback circuit-breaker delay from 5s -> 30s in routing config (route-config: /v1/generate -> fallback-delay-ms = 30000). This reduced flapping between routes.
- 00:45: observed p95 drop back to ~220ms; alert cleared at 00:56.
- 01:10: re-enabled cache-warm job in staged mode (reduced concurrency=2) and monitored eviction rate.

Diagnostics & evidence collected:
- Redis: eviction_count spike + client-side misses correlated with start of cache-warm job. Snapshot: redis-primary-az1 evictions 14k in 5m (link: infra-logs/redis/2026-06-01/00-20).
- Routing logs: multiple rapid route switches for tenants t-104, t-223 (request ids attached in logs).
- GPU autoscale event ids: gpupool-burst-ev-20260601-001 (created instance set +12).
- Heap snapshots and KV cache warm traces uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/handovers/2026-06-01/cache-spike/

Open questions / hypothesis to validate:
- Was cache-warm job misconfigured (concurrency too high) or did memory leak / reduced memory capacity on Redis cause the evictions?
- Why did fallback routing prefer CPU pool so aggressively despite circuit-breaker default settings? (Suspect routing TTL mismatch for 'last-success' metric)

Suggested runbook changes (draft entries to add):
1) Preconditions & immediate checks for cache-eviction spike:
   - Check Redis memory_used, eviction_count, client_miss_rate for last 10m.
   - Command snippets: redis-cli -h $REDIS_HOST INFO memory | grep used_memory; kubectl logs -n infra redis-primary-0 --since=15m | grep evict
2) Temporary mitigations:
   - Pause cache-warm jobs (gcloud scheduler jobs pause <id>) if eviction_count > 1000 / 5m.
   - Increase fallback-delay-ms for affected route to 30000 (config path: /infra/routing/overrides).
   - If GPU pool can scale, enable reserved-burst with capacity bound; include checklist on how to estimate burst size.
3) Post-event items:
   - Replay cache-warm in throttled mode (concurrency=2) and observe for 60m.
   - Collect heap/kv traces and upload to s3 path.
   - File postmortem if tenant-impacted requests > 1% or duration > 30m.

Runbook TODOs (owners):
- Add concrete command snippets for Redis checks (owner: Oliver Grant).
- Add rollback notes for reserved-burst and how to avoid cost surprise (owner: Maya Chen).
- Validate routing metric TTLs and circuit-breaker defaults (owner: Samir Rao).

Follow-ups & action items for daytime team:
- (P0) Confirm whether Redis instance resized earlier today (check infra change log between 18:00-23:59 PDT). If yes, correlate time. (assignee: Maya)
- (P1) Run a controlled cache-warm at low concurrency and watch eviction_count for 2 hours (assignee: Oliver).
- (P1) Create a tiny synthetic load test replicating eviction behavior in staging (assignee: Samir).
- (P2) Draft a short runbook appendix explaining 'fallback-delay-ms' interplay with autoscaler (assignee: Aisha).

Notes for next oncall (handoff):
- If alert SLO-LAT-011 fires again, check eviction_count first; if >1000 in 5m, pause cache-warm job and paged escalations to infrastructure team.
- Avoid immediate toggle of circuit-breakers to <10s — causes flapping. Use 30s for initial mitigation.
- Budget: enabling reserved-burst can incur ~20-30% short term cost; coordinate with billing if extended >2 hours.

Logs & artifacts quick links:
- Alerts: pagerduty incident PD-1187
- Redis logs: infra-logs/redis/2026-06-01/00-20 (s3 link in linked_artifacts)
- GPU autoscale event: gpupool-burst-ev-20260601-001 (cloud console)
- Synthetic trace bundle: s3://redwood-ops/handovers/2026-06-01/cache-spike/trace-bundle.tgz

Appendix: Quick commands used (for record)
- kubectl get hpa -n serving --selector=pool=gpupool -o wide
- gcloud scheduler jobs pause cache-warm-3am --project=infra-prod
- redis-cli -h $REDIS_HOST INFO memory | head -n 20
- curl -sS "https://console.redwood.local/api/metrics?query=latency_ms|route=/v1/generate|p95"

Status at handoff (07:30 PDT):
- System stable, p95 ~210-300ms, all mitigations reverted except runbook config change queued for review.
- Open follow-ups assigned as above and linked in Jira SRE-412.

Quick retrospective notes (observational):
- The cache-warm tooling lacks a backpressure mechanism for Redis capacity — add token-bucket/concurrency enforcement.
- Routing metrics TTLs are too coarse to prevent rapid fallback oscillation on short-lived cache misses.

If you pick this up: please acknowledge in #sre-ops Slack and add your name in the collaborators list here.

-- Aisha P.
extra_notes: This is intended as a working on-call handoff doc; please update runbook-draft branch and link PR in linked_artifacts when ready.
